title: dedicated-autoscaler-burst-util-reporting-v36
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Autoscaler: introduce smoother burst token-bucket smoothing policy to reduce oscillations during rapid load changes.
Throughput guarantees: new per-fleet throughput floor settings and enforcement hooks in allocator.
Utilization reporting: added per-fleet queued_request and burst_consumption metrics; improved dashboards.
Migration: default smoothing enabled for existing fleets; ops can opt out via dedicated.yaml.
description:
Summary:
This PR implements a set of improvements to dedicated fleet autoscaling and utilization reporting focused on smoother burst behavior and stronger throughput guarantees. The change set introduces a token-bucket smoothing policy (configurable) that prevents the autoscaler from rapidly oscillating when short high-traffic spikes occur, plus allocator-level enforcement for per-fleet throughput floors to provide predictable service levels for committed capacity.

Motivation and context:
Customers running Dedicated capacity reported noisy autoscaling during sustained bursty workloads (see ENG-2045). Rapid ramp-ups and immediate releases caused downstream scheduling churn, higher cold-starts, and unexpected cost spikes. We need a conservative smoothing policy on burst allowances and better observability so platform owners can correlate burst consumption with utilization and SLA exposure.

What I changed (high level):
- services/autoscaler: added TokenBucketSmoother (tokenbucket.rs) and plumbed smoothing options into burst control logic (burst_control.rs). Smoothing applies a short-term moving-average to token refill and borrow decisions to reduce oscillation.
- services/fleet-allocator: added throughput_floor enforcement hook during placement decisions. If a fleet has a committed throughput floor, allocator reserves tokens and prefers nodes that satisfy the floor while respecting isolation constraints.
- services/metrics: added new metrics: dedicated_fleet_burst_consumed, dedicated_fleet_burst_remaining, dedicated_fleet_throughput_floor, dedicated_fleet_queued_requests. Updated reporter to emit tags for fleet_id, region, and model_family.
- platform/config: new config knobs in dedicated.yaml: burst_smoothing_enabled, smoothing_alpha, throughput_floor_tokens, throughput_floor_window_seconds.
- docs: added running/dedicated-autoscale.md with configuration examples and migration guidance.
- tests: unit tests for smoothing logic and integration test that simulates burst traffic and validates reduced oscillation and that throughput floors are respected.

Commits:
- Add token-bucket smoothing primitive and tests
- Integrate smoothing into burst controller with config knobs
- Add allocator throughput floor enforcement and coverage tests
- Emit new utilization metrics and update dashboards
- Docs and migration guide
- Fix flake in autoscaler integration test

Files changed (high level):
- services/autoscaler/src/{burst_control.rs,tokenbucket.rs,config.rs,mod.rs}
- services/fleet-allocator/src/{allocator.rs,placement.rs}
- services/metrics/src/utilization_reporter.rs
- platform/config/dedicated.yaml
- docs/running/dedicated-autoscale.md
- tests/integration/autoscaler_burst_test.py
- observability/dashboards/dedicated-util.json

Review conversation (summary):
- Miguel Torres: requested that smoothing be configurable per-fleet and asked for a deterministic backoff for retries when smoothing denies burst. Also asked for clearer invariant comments in tokenbucket.rs. (Addressed in commit 3, added per-fleet override and deterministic retry).
- Renee Zhao: asked for more metrics and tags to make dashboards filterable by allocation strategy; requested retention consideration for cardinality. (Added tags and limited cardinality by model_family + region).
- Devon Lee: flagged potential perf hotspot in allocator when checking throughput_floor across large fleets; suggested caching floor-weighted candidates. (Implemented LRU cache and added unit tests).
- CI initially: integration tests failed on concurrency in autoscaler_burst_test.py due to a race in test harness. I fixed by tightening the harness and adding an exponential backoff for the test's probe loop. Re-ran CI and all checks passed.

Backward compatibility & migration:
- Default: smoothing enabled for new fleets; existing fleets will be softly migrated during a rollout window. Ops can disable smoothing per-fleet via dedicated.yaml or the Console.
- Throughput floors are additive constraints; they will not reduce already-provisioned capacity but may change placement behavior. Documented migration steps in docs/running/dedicated-autoscale.md.

CI & perf:
- Unit test coverage added for smoothing primitives (100% on new modules).
- Integration test simulates a 60s burst and asserts >30% reduction in autoscaler oscillation metric (measured via dedicated_fleet_burst_consumed variance).
- Local perf run shows <2% CPU overhead in allocator path with LRU caching.

Related:
- Linear: ENG-2045, ENG-2100, PM-187
- Related PRs: pr-314159 (burst tokenbucket refactor), pr-314159-dedicated-autoscaler-burst-util-reporting-optimizations.json, pr-362999

Merge notes:
- Squash merge. Please ensure the platform team is notified to update the default config in staging before rollout.

CI status: pass

If merged, follow up with ops to monitor dedicated_fleet_burst_consumed and dedicated_fleet_queued_requests dashboards for the first 72 hours to detect under-provisioning or unexpected throttling.
